REGISTERED ESTABLISHMENT
EXPORT REGISTRATION RECORD
1. Establishment Details
2. Registered Export Operations

This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for chickpeas (pulse). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
3. Registration Status

Registration RE-QLD-2023-0022 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 17 January 2023 and the current registration period extends to 16 January 2026. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person

Dorothy Holt is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2021. The entity is a family trust registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description

The registered premises comprise Lot 28 on Plan DP 777478, located at 22 D'Aguilar Highway, Kingaroy QLD 4610. The total registered area is 29.7 hectares. The registered boundary is delineated on the attached site plan (Appendix A) and includes all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure. Adjoining land parcels and access roads are excluded from the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
6.2 Services and Utilities
6.3 Adjoining Sites

The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow

A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: chickpeas is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities

The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of chickpeas. Total storage capacity is approximately 3,500 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes

No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises

No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

13. Food Safety Program

A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping

Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

5. HACCP Control Chart — Monitoring and Corrective Action
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)

Hygiene and Sanitation Program (THF-HSP-001):
• Pre-season: full clean-down of packhouse — Greefa grader, conveyors, dump tank, wax applicator — using food-safe sanitiser (sodium hypochlorite 200 ppm).
• During season: dump tank water changed every 4 hours; brushes and pads cleaned daily.
• Personnel hygiene: mandatory handwash on entry; clean protective clothing (hairnets, gloves) required in packing area.
• Footwear: boot-wash stations at all packhouse entry points.
• Cleaning schedule: daily wipe-down of packing tables; weekly deep clean of grader lanes; signed Cleaning Register (THF-CLN-01).

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
Waste management procedures for the packhouse (pomace/peel, grading rejects, wastewater from dump tank, wax residue, packaging waste) are NOT included in this HACCP plan.
ACTION REQUIRED: Document waste streams, disposal methods, frequency and records in accordance with Rules s4-7A(2)(a) and DAFF Performance Standards Element 3.1.
Interim note: Packhouse rejects are currently collected by a local livestock farmer. No written procedure or records are maintained.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
No formal pest control program is documented for Esperance Bay Exports Pty Ltd. No bait station map, monitoring schedule, contractor engagement or corrective action procedures are included.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)

Traceability System (THF-TRACE-001):
• Grower–lot–bin system: each field bin labelled with grower ID, orchard block, variety, harvest date.
• Packing records: each packing run assigned a lot code (grower–date–variety–run); printed on carton label.
• Dispatch: dispatch register links lot code → transport vehicle rego → cold store allocation → destination.
• Recall readiness: lot trace exercise conducted annually; 4-hour trace commitment.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
Product flow chart: see Section 3 Process Flow Diagram.

Failed Goods Procedure (THF-FGP-001):
• Lots failing pesticide residue test: placed on HOLD; grower notified; DAFF notified; lot destroyed or returned to grower for domestic use.
• Lots failing codling moth inspection: rejected from export; cold treatment applied; re-inspected before any re-presentation.
• Metal detector rejects: carton quarantined; inspected; source identified; disposed if contaminated.
• Records: all non-conformances logged in THF-NCR register.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)

Phytosanitary Security (THF-PSP-001):
• Export-cleared fruit stored in dedicated cool store cells (CC-3 and CC-4); not co-mingled with domestic-grade fruit.
• Cartons labelled with lot code before storage; label integrity checked before dispatch.
• Packing materials (trays, cartons) stored in sealed room; not accessible to rodents or birds.
• DAFF phytosanitary certificate issued per consignment after sampling.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.
HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance.

FARM MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. OVERVIEW

Burnett River Chickpea is a registered export establishment located at 22 D'Aguilar Highway, Kingaroy QLD 4610, QLD. The establishment holds RE Number RE-QLD-2023-0022 and is registered to handle and export Specialty Crops under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2. BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
3. EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
4. FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1 Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)

The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Specialty Crops.
4.2 Lighting (C2)
LED panel lighting installed 2020: 500 lux (processing), 400 lux (storage), 380 lux (load-out). IP65-rated food-grade fittings. Annual lux-level verification by licensed electrician.
4.3 Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)

Amenities block within 20 m of processing floor: 1 toilet, 1 hand basin hot/cold water, liquid soap, paper towels. Separate no-touch basin and hand sanitiser dispenser installed at cool store/packing area access point, as required by site hygiene protocol.
5. DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1 Cleanability (C4)

All product-contact and grain-contact surfaces are smooth, non-porous and cleanable: 3-coat epoxy floor system; FRP (fibreglass-reinforced panel) wall linings to 2.7 m; stainless-steel equipment internals. Conveyor and auger housings have hinged access panels. Full washdown of product-contact surfaces required between commodity lots per cleaning SOP.
5.2 Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)

Design features minimising pest entry: smooth wall surfaces; all roof-wall junctions factory-sealed; cable/pipe penetrations sealed with food-grade silicone; 6 mm mesh on all fixed ventilation louvres; self-closing personnel doors with magnetic seals; roller doors serviced annually to maintain threshold seal integrity; no open drainage channels.
5.3 Waste Disposal Design (C6)

Contained waste management infrastructure: liquid drains to bunded sump (2000 L) outside the processing building; solid waste in sealed wheeled bins with lids; external waste bay roofed and bunded on three sides with 300 mm concrete kerb and sealed slab. Organic waste composted in covered bay 30 m from processing. No open waste storage areas.
6. WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1 Waste Management Procedures (C7)

Establishment Waste Management Plan (EWMP v3.0, reviewed April 2025): details procedures for all waste streams — product spillage, packaging, liquid washdown, chemical containers and dust. Scheduled tasks on daily operations checklist, signed off by shift supervisor. Records retained 3 years minimum.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
7. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1 Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)

The establishment is maintained in a clean and hygienic condition appropriate for export of Specialty Crops. All product-contact surfaces are cleaned between commodity lots using the documented cleaning procedure. Non-product-contact surfaces cleaned on a 8-weekly schedule. No hygiene deficiencies at most recent inspection.
7.2 Pest Condition (C9)

Fruit fly (Drosophila spp.) activity noted in the fresh waste holding area adjacent to the packing line. Population levels in the waste area are high (>100 individuals observed during a 5-minute observation). Adults observed moving from the waste area to the packing conveyor during peak heat of day. Daily waste removal is insufficient to control population during current season peak.

HYGIENE & SANITATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. ESTABLISHMENT INFORMATION
2. SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment

This plan covers all areas of Burnett River Chickpea used in nut processing and packing operations for export Almonds. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Almonds during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3. PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
4. MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
5. AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival / Intake Area

Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Receival / Intake Area in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Huller / Cracker / Sheller

After each production run: Power off and lock out drive before opening. Dismantle outer access panels. Remove nut residue, shell fragments, and skin from rollers, screens, and internal surfaces using a stiff brush. Prepare BioDegreaser FD at 1:25. Apply to metal surfaces where oil residue is present. Contact time 5 minutes. Rinse with water. Allow to dry before reassembly. Record in Equipment Cleaning Log.
Grading & Sizing Equipment

After each run: Clear all nut product from grading screens and conveyor belts. Brush screens using designated nut-cleaning brush to remove embedded skins and fragments. Prepare EnzymeClear at 1:20 in a spray bottle. Spray conveyor belt and rollers. Wipe with clean cloth. Inspect for any remaining organic residue. Record in Run Record.
Drying Area / Pads / Dryer

Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Drying Area / Pads / Dryer in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Storage Bins / Holding Area

Between commodity lots: Inspect and clean storage bins before loading a new nut commodity. Using industrial vacuum, remove all residual nut material from bin walls, seams, and floor. Inspect for pest activity (insect frass, rodent droppings). Storage Manager signs pre-loading checklist confirming bin is clean and free of pests.
6. MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES

Dead-stock zones include the inner drum of hulling and cracking equipment, under-belt spaces on grading conveyors, and the floor beneath dryer trays. Nut oil residue and fine skin particles accumulate in these areas and require periodic disassembly cleaning.
7. APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
8. RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1 Record System

Cleaning records are maintained using a combination of paper log sheets and digital entries in the site management system. All records are retained at site for a minimum of two years from the date of completion.
8.2 Sanitation Verification Log Template
9. VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
Independent third-party hygiene audits are conducted twice annually. Between audits, internal verification is carried out by the establishment manager using a standardised checklist.
10. NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION

Non-conformances with cleaning requirements are recorded in the site's corrective action log. Root cause analysis is completed for any repeat event within 30 days. Completed corrective actions are verified by the manager and signed off before closure.
11. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)

Routine inspection of Burnett River Chickpea completed on 6 March 2025. All areas assessed as compliant with the hygiene standards required for the export of Almonds. Cleaning logs current and records up to date.
